notes:
Stage: mid-market SaaS (product analytics + in-app help).

Quick summary: evaluating Redwood Hosted API first to validate embeddings quality and query latency for in-app semantic search; then plan limited Dedicated POC for predictable throughput (evening batch jobs + peak traffic). Primary driver: reduce token/unit cost while improving recall + reranking for product help search.

Recent activity / timeline:
- 2026-02-12: Intro call (AE Maya) — product overview, initial requirements capture. Client: product + infra leads (CTO: L. Morales).
- 2026-02-18: Tech deep-dive with SE Jordan — discussed vector DB integration (self-hosted Postgres+pgvector vs Pinecone), batching for nightly indexing, cold-start cheap fallback. Fireflies: ff_2026_02_25_01.
- 2026-02-25: Demo of Hosted API — fast onboarding, embeddings quality check using sample KB (internal docs). Follow-up: provide benchmark runbook and sample python batch job. Gmail thread: gmail_thread_17c2_0226.
- 2026-03-03: POC kickoff — 2-week POC: 1) embeddings evaluation on 250k docs; 2) end-to-end latency SLO tests (95p latency target 150ms for 1kqps sim); 3) integration test with Postgres+pgvector. Fireflies: ff_2026_03_03_02.
- 2026-03-09: Mid-POC sync — initial embeddings precision good; throughput bottleneck observed during batch ingest (memory pressure on batch workers). Action: Redwood Optimize suggestions requested + batching parameter tuning.

Use-case & technical requirements (client notes):
- Workload: bursty product search traffic (peaks at release nights), scheduled nightly bulk embedding jobs for new docs, semantic reranking for in-app help articles.
- Targets: 95th percentile query latency < 150ms for single-vector nearest neighbor + re-rank (hosted) and < 120ms on Dedicated with KV cache enabled.
- Throughput: sustained 800 qps during product peak window; nightly ingest throughput ~200k docs over 6 hours.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market; wants predictable monthly commit if Dedicated is chosen. Target ARR economics: stay under $120k/year for search stack.
- Vector DB: preference for Pgvector currently; evaluating Pinecone for managed option. Must support bulk upserts and compressed vector formats.
- Fault tolerance: want automated fallback to smaller model variant when capacity constrained.
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency traces required for internal chargeback.
- Compliance: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for encryption-at-rest, ability to set EU data residency for EU users.

POC findings so far (SE notes):
- Embedding quality: Redwood curated open models slightly outscore our current baseline on NDCG@10 for help-article retrieval tests (+6%).
- Batch ingest: current batch workers hit memory pressure around 50k doc window; suggested changes: increase chunking, stream writes to pgvector, use Optimize's batching profile.
- Latency: Hosted API meets sub-150ms median, but 95p spikes during simulated peak; Dedicated expected to solve with reserved GPUs + KV cache.

Commercial / procurement notes:
- Wants clear pricing for: Hosted monthly usage, Dedicated reserved commit tiers (3/6/12 months), burst credits.
- Asks: committed monthly capacity pricing, breakouts for embeddings vs generation cost, enterprise support uplift. Drive: pricing deck link.
- Legal: needs data residency clause and SOC2 attestation attached to contract. Blocker: legal wants sample DPA + residency guarantee.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- "Embedding quality is better than we expected — improves recall on long-tail queries." — Product Lead (S. Iqbal)
- "Need predictable monthly costs — we cannot have highly variable token bills during release cycles." — CFO (M. Hernandez)

Next steps (short):
- 2026-03-15: internal POC results review w/ AE + SE to finalize numbers (scheduled).
- Provide Dedicated pricing scenarios (3-tier commit) + migration playbook from Hosted -> Dedicated.
- Share sample DPA + SOC2 certs with legal.
- Run Optimize tuning for batch ingest and re-run nightly ingest test (aim: stable throughput + <20% cost reduction).

Open blockers (quick list): legal/DPA, residency SLA, Dedicated burst SLA clarity, final ARR budget approval by procurement.

Stubs / links used in notes: pricing deck (https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Pricing-Deck-ThriveFlow), POC runbook (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ThriveFlow-POC-Docs), Fireflies meeting IDs ff_2026_02_25_01 and ff_2026_03_03_02, Gmail threads gmail_thread_17c2_0226 and gmail_thread_12b9_0304, Jira INF-4729.
